title: Container Bookings: Shipping Instruction and VGM Cut-Offs and Grace
content:
Every sailing of a Container Bookings booking has a cut-off for shipping instructions (SI) and a cut-off for the SOLAS verified gross mass (VGM). This page states how those cut-offs and their grace work.

## Clauses in force

1. Each document has its own deadline on the allocated sailing: the shipping instructions are due by that sailing's SI cut-off, and the VGM by its VGM cut-off.
2. Shipping instructions are accepted for the allocated vessel only if they arrive no later than the SI cut-off extended by the product's SI grace hours. That grace deadline is the SI cut-off time moved forward by the grace hours, each hour a full sixty minutes, reckoned in the local time of the port of loading; instructions arriving at the deadline exactly are still within it. The cut-off and the receipt moment are read from the booking record.
3. Instructions that arrive after the SI cut-off but within grace give rise to one late shipping-instruction entry for the booking, at the product's late SI fee. Instructions arriving after grace are not accepted for that sailing: the booking is rolled to the following sailing as a roll caused by the customer, and no late fee is charged for the sailing that was missed.
4. A VGM that arrives after the VGM cut-off but no later than that cut-off extended by the product's VGM grace hours gives rise to one late VGM entry. Because no container is loaded without a VGM, a VGM later than grace likewise leads to a roll caused by the customer.
5. Each late submission is recorded as an entry of its own.
6. A late documentation fee may be entered only while the booking's status is confirmed, equipment released or gated in.
7. Documents that arrive on time give rise to nothing.

## Clauses no longer in force

- The former rule that set a late entry at 0.00 while the customer's late-document count across all of its bookings over a trailing 365-day period stayed under the free allowance, and at the full fee otherwise, is no longer in force; the free allowance is now applied under the current late-document recording basis of Container Bookings.
- The former rule that priced the late VGM entry on the booking's full container quantity is no longer in force; the VGM fee is now reckoned under the current late VGM recording basis.

## Grace boundary cases (hypothetical times, port-of-loading local time)

| SI cut-off | Grace hours | Receipt | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| day D, 14:00 | 24 | day D, 13:50 | on time; nothing entered |
| day D, 14:00 | 24 | day D plus one, 14:00 | late but within grace |
| day D, 14:00 | 24 | day D plus one, 14:01 | outside grace; not accepted for this sailing |

The same arithmetic applies to the VGM, using the VGM cut-off and the product's VGM grace hours. The times and the grace figure are invented for the illustration.
